item.title: Former juvenile jail superintendent lived in Chicago, report says
item.description: Injustice Watch reported last year that Leonard Dixon owned property and voted in Michigan.

item.title: No contest: Cook County judicial primary elections draw dwindling field of candidates
item.description: For the second straight primary season, more than half the races for Cook County circuit judge on the March 17 ballot are uncontested, with just 45 candidates vying for 28 open seats.

item.title: Where to find a copy of Injustice Watch’s judicial election guide for the 2026 primary
item.description: We printed 170,000 copies of our judicial election guide for the March 17 primary elections and distributed them across Cook County. Here’s where you can find them.

item.title: Why is the Cook County State’s Attorney prosecuting nonviolent ICE protesters?
item.description: A Block Club Chicago investigation found dozens of protesters arrested by state police are still facing criminal charges for minor infractions, such as sitting on a concrete barrier — even after Gov. JB Pritzker vowed to protect their First Amendment rights.

item.title: The King of Liens
item.description: Tax buyer Greg Bingham has amassed hundreds of tax-foreclosed properties in Cook County since the 1990s. Along the way, he’s been dogged by allegations of fraud, an Injustice Watch investigation found.

item.title: What makes these judicial races on Chicago’s South Side unique?
item.description: This year, fewer judicial candidates are running overall, either countywide or in a subcircuit. But voters in the South Loop, Hyde Park, South Shore and Roseland neighborhoods are choosing from an unusually crowded field for two open seats.

item.title: March 2026 Cook County Judicial Election Guide | Injustice Watch
item.description: Injustice Watch's guide to the March 2026 Cook County judicial primary elections.

item.title: Judicial election results: Three appointed judges rejected by voters in Cook County judicial primaries
item.description: Voters had no choice in more than half the races, which were uncontested. Several candidates won despite negative ratings from local bar groups.

item.title: State forensic science commission blasts UIC over rogue crime lab
item.description: The Illinois Forensic Science Commission called on the university to conduct a proper audit of its lab, which has been responsible for nearly two dozen wrongful DUI convictions.
